The RSL framework combines symbolic regression with deep reinforcement learning to predict turbine blade fatigue life.
The RSL method was evaluated on two turbine blade materials: GH4169 and TC4.
The RSL method produced more accurate and interpretable predictive formulas compared to six empirical formulas and five machine learning algorithms.

The RSL framework incorporates logical constraints, such as dimension removal, arity tracking, and function enforcement, to ensure the generated formulas are structurally valid and aligned with physical laws.
The deep reinforcement learning component of RSL uses a Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) to guide the symbolic regression process towards more accurate and generalizable predictive models.
Finite element simulations were conducted to assess mechanical properties at critical points on the turbine blades and predict fatigue life under various operating conditions.
The RSL method demonstrated superior or comparable predictive performance to both empirical formulas and machine learning models for the GH4169 and TC4 turbine blade materials.

Traditional empirical formulas for fatigue life prediction, such as the Coffin-Manson, BM, KBM, FS, and WHS criteria, rely on mechanical properties like tensile strength, ductility, hardness, and strain components.

One of the key challenges in predicting turbine blade fatigue life is the inherent complexity of failure mechanisms and the microscopic scale of crack initiation, which make defect detection challenging.
The RSL method addresses the limitations of traditional approaches by generating interpretable predictive formulas that are aligned with physical laws and principles.
The incorporation of logical constraints and deep reinforcement learning in the RSL framework significantly improves the efficiency and performance of the symbolic regression process.

The RSL method demonstrates the potential of combining symbolic regression and deep reinforcement learning to derive accurate, interpretable, and physically meaningful predictive models for critical engineering applications.
The RSL framework offers a novel approach for advancing research on the fatigue life prediction of critical components in aircraft engines.
The paper highlights the importance of accurate and efficient prediction of turbine blade fatigue life for ensuring the safety and reliability of aircraft engines.

The RSL method's ability to generate interpretable formulas that capture the intrinsic relationship between material properties and fatigue life is a key advantage over traditional black-box machine learning models.
